title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## AA‑Robotics v0.1 Benchmark

### The Breakthrough
A new benchmark gives zero‑shot access to a Hiwonder NexArm robot via a simple HTTP API, four external cameras, and a coding‑agent container. GPT‑16 Astra achieved the highest score of 69 out of 100 while costing $16.36 per task, revealing that frontier language models are still slower and more expensive than humans.

### The Caveats
The benchmark only evaluates eight simple tabletop tasks on a single robot arm, so it provides no evidence that frontier language models can handle more complex manipulations or generalize across different hardware setups.

## Graph‑Reweighted Behavior Cloning (GR‑BC)

### The Breakthrough
GR‑BC builds a goal‑reachability graph from demonstrations and human‑intervened rollouts, weighting action chunks by their contribution to success. The method attains 91% success on four precise manipulation tasks after only a few offline iterations and works across three VLA backbones without extra critics.

### The Caveats
The work compares against only a single‑round supervised fine‑tuning baseline, leaving it unknown whether GR‑BC truly beats stronger reward‑model or reinforcement‑learning methods.

## Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning (HiRe‑MoMa)

### The Breakthrough
HiRe‑MoMa fine‑tunes a frozen mobile‑manipulation base policy with separate residual heads for the base and arm, using sparse human interventions (<20% of steps). With roughly 30 minutes of online data it improves real‑world task performance, demonstrating a practical way to adapt complex systems on‑robot.

### The Caveats
The paper reports performance gains but provides no comparison against any existing fine‑tuning or residual‑learning baselines, leaving the claimed improvement unverified.

## Diffusion‑Generated Humanoid Controllers

### The Breakthrough
A latent diffusion model trained on compressed actor‑network weights can be sampled to generate functional humanoid controllers, which were deployed on a Unitree G1 robot to walk, dance and perform a spin kick. Analysis of the latent space reveals a consistent kinematic prior in the first‑layer weights.

### The Caveats
The paper never compares its diffusion‑generated controllers to any existing generative or policy‑learning baselines, so the claimed advantage over prior methods remains unsubstantiated.

## Tiered‑Resolution Volumetric Mapping

### The Breakthrough
A single map structure stores fine resolution only near the robot’s planned corridor and coarse resolution elsewhere, cutting map size by 13–15× and integration CPU time by 6–8× while keeping navigation quality comparable to full‑resolution maps. Evaluated on two real‑world outdoor teleoperation datasets.

### The Caveats
The claimed real‑time planning‑mapping performance is only demonstrated offline on recorded datasets, with no live robot deployment to confirm the approach works under real‑world timing and feedback conditions.

## lidar_slam_ros2 (ROS2 LiDAR SLAM)

### The Breakthrough
The ROS2 package pairs the RKO‑LIO front‑end with a graph‑based backend, achieving 99.7% scan tracking and 0.55 mm RMSE APE on the Koide Hard outdoor dataset, and runs faster than real time (factor 0.44) while outputting Autoware‑compatible map bundles.

### The Caveats
The reported tracking rate and RMSE are shown only on a single dataset with no baseline SLAM systems for comparison, leaving the claimed performance unsubstantiated.

## OOMWOO Open‑Source Robot Vacuum

### The Breakthrough
The project provides complete hardware designs, firmware, and a ROS2‑based navigation stack (Nav2) with a modular micro‑ROS firmware architecture, plus a Gazebo URDF simulation that lets developers test cleaning logic, SLAM and Home Assistant integration without any physical robot.

### The Caveats
No physical robot has been built or evaluated, so claims about real‑world performance, privacy, and modularity remain unproven.

## lampOS Open‑Source OS for Physical AI

### The Breakthrough
lampOS is a Python‑based operating system that integrates LLM agents (Hermes, Claude‑Code, Codex) with robot hardware via a modular skill framework, intent routing and runtime hooks, supporting voice, vision and motor control and a BYOR workflow; the repo has 455 stars.

### The Caveats
The repository offers no empirical evaluation or baseline comparisons, so the claimed general‑purpose OS capabilities remain unverified.

### Priority
The AA‑Robotics benchmark provides the first quantitative comparison of frontier LLMs on a real robot arm, setting a clear yardstick for embodied AI progress.

### One action
Track the AA‑Robotics leaderboard and consider using its API to evaluate your own LLM‑controlled robot experiments.
